column1: preamble
column2: *The fewest questions that settle one thing — who the tool is for — and, traced downward, the same roots are the design explained.

column1: preamble
column2: Read them forward to decide fit; read them down to see why it is built this way.*

column2: > Where this comes from: twenty years of wrestling with the *full geotag* problem.

column1: What this is
column2: The structure here — the numbered folder workspace, the JSON files, the mandatory re-prep, the plan/validate/execute ceremony — is the direct, more or less inevitable consequence of a few root facts/decisions, and the point of laying them out here is economy: ask the **smallest set of questions that settles fit**, so one can quickly decide if this is for them.

column2: The roots are what is open to debate; the rest follows from them.

column1: What this is
column2: **If one accepts the roots, the architecture is largely not negotiable; if one rejects them, one is simply not the intended user — and in neither case are the downstream details the place to start.**

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | F1 | **A photo batch is large — thousands of frames, several cameras.** | A trip dump or a years-deep library is big and mixed: many RAW/JPEG frames across multiple cameras and phones. | The card one keeps meaning to deal with; the decade of folders; or *"I'll geotag these someday."* |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | F2 | **Camera clocks drift — independently, and from day to day.** | Each body's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes between days (drift, manual resets to local time in the morning, missed DST). There is no single global offset to find. | The import that landed an hour early; the shots an hour off after a border; a day's frames scattered because the clock was never set — blamed on negligence or forgetfulness, not on a category. |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | F3 | **GPX coverage is partial.** | The logger's tracks reach *some* of the library, never all of it — so the track alone can never place every frame; the rest needs fallbacks. | The half-tagged library; the map view with holes where phone-sync missed; the frames that came with a pin and the many that didn't. |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | P1 | **Photos matter; they are irreplaceable, so they deserve care.** | Value | Because they matter, no original may be lost or silently altered — correctness beats convenience. |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | P2 | **A local, owned, folder-based library.** | Choice | The destination is a plain directory tree on disk (feeds digiKam or Immich), not a cloud service or proprietary catalog. |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | P3 | **Ask only what the data can't settle.** | Design value | Resolve everything derivable automatically; ask only real judgment questions, and make each one cheap to answer. |

column1: The root layer: three facts, four choices
column2: | P4 | **100% placement, even under GPS scarcity.** | Goal | Every photo ends up on the map — precise where tracks allow, rough or manual where they don't — so the result is a *map-complete* library, not just the frames that came with a location. |

column2: Because each camera's clock is wrong by its own amount, and that amount changes from day to day (F2), there is no single offset to discover — the correct answer is **per (camera group, destination, day)**.

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: *That* granularity is the entire source of the decisions' "complexity": it is a consequence of real, time-varying drift, not a premise.

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: Such intricacy would be brutal to enter by hand, so P3 (ask only what the data can't settle) governs how it is collected — and introduces the document's central trade.

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | Drift is per-camera and per-day, so no global offset is correct | The offset is **inferred and applied per (camera group, destination, day)**; corrections fall *between* destinations, never within one — which is why **one destination = one coherent shoot** |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | Intricate, evidence-specific decisions are too error-prone to hand-edit | **Format + editor split**: JSON is the record; the Time/Drift/GPS app is what writes it |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | The record must stay an honest statement of *intent*, not a mutable scratchpad | The editor writes **only the `user_decision` field** — never derived or evidence fields |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | Asking per-photo would be thousands of short-reaching chores | Decisions **cascade**: *one far-reaching choice high in the tree is traded for many short-reaching ones* — inherit unless overridden, remembered across re-runs. (This is where "far-reaching" comes from — a chosen trade, not an inherent property.) |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | Inheritance needs an axis to travel along | The destination tree must be a **hierarchy** — the cascade rides on folder nesting, so a flat or tag-based layout can't inherit at all, and every value would fall back to per-photo entry |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | The unavoidable human act should pay for itself | Timezone, clock offset, and GPS fallback are **piggybacked on the destination sort** one would do anyway for real albums (P2) |

column1: From F2 + P3 — drift makes the decisions intricate; P3 keeps them cheap
column2: | The tedious part of a judgment call should be pre-computed | **Camera groups are generated for the user**, ready to paste — leaving only the judgment, not the derivation |

column1: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
column2: | Placement cannot depend on the track alone | A **cascading folder-level GPS fallback** — set one coordinate at a trip's root and it is inherited down the tree (P3 makes this cheap; one answer covers many photos) |

column1: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
column2: | The true unplaceable set must be surfaced, never silently dropped | An explicit, short **remainder worklist** — what no evidence can locate is collected for a manual pin, not left off the map |

column1: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
column2: | Every placeable point of the track must be squeezed out | **Direct match → interpolation between points → bounded extrapolation off the ends**, each used before falling back to manual |

column1: From P4 — total placement under GPS scarcity
